chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Piano at home and his father's job as head janitor
summary: A piano was in the parlor but nobody used it; he played by ear, took brief lessons, and describes his father's work at South Station and his mother's day work.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Before that, though, had you been interested in playing anything at all at school or anything?
Not in music. Nothing. I played baseball and games, and one thing or another.
You had a piano at home?
Oh, there was always a piano there. My Daddy tried to start the kids off musically, you know. Because at that time, practically all homes had a piano in it.
There was no radio or television or nothing like that. But practically in all the homes there was a piano.
In your home did anybody play it?

No. I played about as much as anybody in the family. He started my two oldest brothers and my sister with lessons on the piano. But nothing ever happened. My brother, he'd be out in the street playing ball or something. They cared nothin' about the piano. And then I
would come along, and I would play by ear, you know. I'd be trying to pick out something.

They started me with piano lessons, but I didn't keep them up, because I wasn't interested in the piano then. I wanted a saxophone! Well, my Daddy... Pianos were never cheap. Pianos were always expensive. And with the salary that he was making, how he could ever afford to buy a piano I don't know!

He was the chief of the what would you call it...? The maintenance... That's what they would call them today. In them days he was just a chief janitor. He was the head janitor at South Station, where the trains come in. He was the head janitor there, up in the building. He had two floors up there. He was the Boss Man up there. And salaries was no big deal in them days. I mean...
She did a day's work. Not wholly. But she had a family to raise. Every time you'd turn around, Mama was... You know what I mean? The family was getting bigger. All right?
So I don't know, well... I forgot where I was at...
